sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    LB[load balancer] --> R[readiness /readyz: 200?]
    R -->|yes| ROUTE[route traffic]
    R -->|no| REMOVE[stop routing — no restart]
    ORCH[orchestrator] --> L[liveness /healthz: 200?]
    L -->|no| RESTART[restart container]
    L -->|yes| UP[process is alive]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The kubelet probe mechanics (the Kubernetes side): the livenessProbe and readinessProbe in the pod spec — the kubelet polls the endpoint on the interval; failures count against the failureThreshold; crossing it triggers the action (restart for liveness, remove from service for readiness). The initial delay (the startup grace) and the timeout (the probe's own deadline) are the tuning.

The anti-patterns the question tests for: (1) the liveness probe that checks the DB (restarts cascade); (2) the readiness with no dependency check (routes traffic to a pod that can't serve — the check that's always 200 is a decorative readiness); (3) the health endpoint that allocates or logs on every request (the probe traffic is constant — the endpoint is the hottest route).

The Go-specific pattern: the health mux mount WITHOUT middleware (auth on the health path = the probe gets a 401 = the loop). The dedicated listener (a second port for health/monitoring — the admin port) isolates health from the main service's middleware stack.
